message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"1","text":"Clement to James, the lord and bishop of bishops, who governs the holy Jerusalem church of the Hebrews and the churches everywhere that have been well established by God’s providence, together with the elders and deacons and all the other brothers: may peace always be.\n\nLet it be known to you, my lord, that Simon—who, because of his true faith and the most secure basis of his teaching, was designated to be the foundation of the church and, for this very reason, was renamed Peter by Jesus himself with his unlying mouth; the firstfruits of our Lord; the first of the apostles; the one to whom the Father first revealed the Son; the one whom the Messiah rightly pronounced blessed; the called and chosen one, table companion and fellow traveler; the good and proven disciple; the one commanded to illuminate the West, the darker part of the world, as more capable than everyone else, and who proved able to accomplish it; and indeed, how long shall I prolong the account, unwilling to disclose the painful thing that necessity compels me, even if late, in any event to tell?—this same man, because of his boundless affection for humanity, having clearly and publicly proclaimed to the whole world, under the present evil one, the good king who was to come, and having come as far as here, to Rome, saving people through teaching willed by God, himself left this present life through violence.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὴν Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἁγίαν Ἑβραίων ἐκκλησίαν","chosen":"the holy Jerusalem church of the Hebrews","rationale":"Preserves Jerusalem as the church’s location or identifying designation and retains its explicit association with the Hebrews."},{"source_quote":"τὴν ἀσφαλεστάτην αὐτοῦ τῆς διδασκαλίας ὑπόθεσιν","chosen":"the most secure basis of his teaching","rationale":"Renders ὑπόθεσις as the underlying basis of the teaching and preserves the superlative force of ἀσφαλεστάτην."},{"source_quote":"ἀψευδεῖ στόματι","chosen":"with his unlying mouth","rationale":"Keeps the source’s concrete image and its claim that Jesus’ naming was free from falsehood."},{"source_quote":"ὁ χριστὸς","chosen":"the Messiah","rationale":"Χριστός functions independently as a title here rather than as part of the name Jesus Christ."},{"source_quote":"οὗτος αὐτὸς","chosen":"this same man","rationale":"Marks the emphatic resumption of Simon after the extended series of descriptions and the intervening rhetorical question."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ τοῦ ἐνεστῶτος πονηροῦ","chosen":"under the present evil one","rationale":"With the genitive, ἐπί is taken temporally as locating the proclamation under the ascendancy of a personal evil figure; a more impersonal reading, ‘amid the present evil,’ remains possible."},{"source_quote":"θεοβουλήτῳ διδασκαλίᾳ","chosen":"through teaching willed by God","rationale":"Renders θεοβούλητος as describing teaching that accords with or proceeds from God’s will."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ νῦν βίου βιαίως τὸ ζῆν μετήλλαξεν","chosen":"left this present life through violence","rationale":"Communicates the death denoted by the exchange-language while retaining the explicit claim that the departure from life was violent; μετήλλαξεν literally depicts an exchange or change, without naming what was received in exchange."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"καὶ δὴ μέχρι ποῦ· μηκύνω τὸν λόγον, μὴ βουλόμενος σημῆναι τὸ λυποῦν, ὃ ἐξ ἀνάγκης κἂν βραδὺ πάντως εἰπεῖν με δεῖ;","issue":"The printed high point after μέχρι ποῦ interrupts the interrogative phrase from its verb μηκύνω, leaving the exact scope of the rhetorical question editorially uncertain. The translation provisionally takes the words together as a rhetorical interruption within the larger sentence about Simon; the punctuation is a confirmed editorial feature, not evidence of source corruption.","proposed_reading":"καὶ δὴ μέχρι ποῦ μηκύνω τὸν λόγον, μὴ βουλόμενος σημῆναι τὸ λυποῦν, ὃ ἐξ ἀνάγκης κἂν βραδὺ πάντως εἰπεῖν με δεῖ;","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"2","text":"Now, in the very days when he was about to die, after the brothers had assembled, he suddenly took hold of my hand, stood up before the church, and said, “Listen to me, brothers and fellow servants. Since—as I was taught by the Lord and Teacher Jesus Christ, who sent me—the days of my death have drawn near, I ordain this Clement as bishop for you. To him I entrust my chair of teaching. He accompanied me from the beginning to the end and thus listened to all my discourses; to speak in summary, he shared in all my trials and was found persevering in faith. More than anyone else, I have found by experience that he is God-revering, a lover of humanity, pure, widely learned, self-controlled, good, just, patient, and knows how to bear bravely the acts of ingratitude committed by some of those receiving instruction. Therefore I impart to him the authority to bind and release, so that, concerning whatever he ordains on earth, it will stand decreed in the heavens. For he will bind what must be bound and release what must be released, since he knows the church’s rule. Listen to him, therefore, recognizing that whoever grieves the one who presides over truth sins against the Messiah and provokes the Father of all; for this reason, that person will not live. Therefore the one who presides must himself occupy the place of a physician, not possess the rage of an irrational beast.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"σύνδουλοι","chosen":"fellow servants","rationale":"Retains the shared servant status expressed by the compound rather than reducing it to a general term for colleagues."},{"source_quote":"ᾧ τὴν ἐμὴν τῶν λόγων πιστεύω καθέδραν","chosen":"To him I entrust my chair of teaching","rationale":"Preserves the institutional chair image while taking τῶν λόγων to characterize it as the chair associated with Peter’s words or teaching."},{"source_quote":"συνελὼν ἐρῶ","chosen":"to speak in summary","rationale":"Conveys the idiom’s transition from the preceding details to a concise characterization."},{"source_quote":"φιλάνθρωπον","chosen":"a lover of humanity","rationale":"Preserves the word’s explicit orientation toward human beings rather than narrowing it to generic kindness."},{"source_quote":"τῶν κατηχουμένων","chosen":"those receiving instruction","rationale":"Conveys the participle’s sense without requiring the later technical loanword ‘catechumens.’"},{"source_quote":"τοῦ δεσμεύειν καὶ λύειν","chosen":"to bind and release","rationale":"Keeps the paired judicial and disciplinary imagery while distinguishing λύειν from merely untying a physical object."},{"source_quote":"περὶ παντὸς οὗ ἂν χειροτονήσῃ","chosen":"concerning whatever he ordains","rationale":"Restores the explicit περὶ, ‘concerning,’ and keeps χειροτονέω visibly connected with the earlier ‘I ordain.’ The phrase may instead refer personally to ‘anyone he appoints.’"},{"source_quote":"ἔσται δεδογματισμένον ἐν οὐρανοῖς","chosen":"it will stand decreed in the heavens","rationale":"Preserves the established-decree sense of δεδογματισμένον without directly identifying the object of Clement’s earthly action with the heavenly decree."},{"source_quote":"ἰατροῦ τόπον ἐπέχειν","chosen":"occupy the place of a physician","rationale":"Retains the contrast between healing authority and the rage of an irrational beast."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἵνα περὶ παντὸς οὗ ἂν χειροτονήσῃ ἐπὶ γῆς ἔσται δεδογματισμένον ἐν οὐρανοῖς","issue":"The gender and reference of παντὸς οὗ and the semantic range of χειροτονέω permit both an impersonal interpretation, ‘concerning whatever he ordains on earth,’ and a personal interpretation, ‘concerning anyone he appoints on earth.’ The main translation provisionally adopts the former while preserving περὶ and the recurrence of the ordination verb; neither interpretation is uniquely established by the supplied wording.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"3","text":"As he was saying these things, I fell before him and pleaded with him, declining the honor and authority of the chair. But he answered, “Do not ask this of me, for I have resolved that this should happen—and all the more for this very reason, if you decline it—because such a chair does not need a rash man eager to occupy the chair, but one who is circumspect in character and widely learned in discourse. Produce someone better, one who accompanied me more than you, listened to my words, and thoroughly learned the governance of the church, and I will not force you, against your will, to do what is right. But you will not now be able to produce anyone better than yourself, for you are the superior firstfruit of the nations being saved through me. Nevertheless, consider this other point as well: if, fearing the danger of sin, you do not undertake the governance of the church, know well that you sin more, since, though able to help those who revere God, as people sailing and in danger, you refuse, considering only your own interest and not what benefits everyone in common. I know with certainty that you must in every case undertake the danger, since I do not cease asking this of you for the help of everyone. Therefore, the sooner you agree with me, the more you will relieve me of discouragement.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"παραιτούμενος τὴν τῆς καθέδρας τιμήν τε καὶ ἐξουσίαν","chosen":"declining the honor and authority of the chair","rationale":"Preserves Clement’s refusal of both the office’s honor and its governing power."},{"source_quote":"φιλοκαθεδροῦντος τολμηροῦ","chosen":"a rash man eager to occupy the chair","rationale":"Conveys the coined expression’s criticism of someone recklessly ambitious for the presiding seat."},{"source_quote":"εὐλαβοῦς τὸν τρόπον καὶ πολυμαθοῦς τὸν λόγον","chosen":"circumspect in character and widely learned in discourse","rationale":"The context contrasts reckless ambition with cautious character and extensive competence in teaching or discourse."},{"source_quote":"δὸς δὲ τὸν κρείττονα","chosen":"Produce someone better","rationale":"The imperative challenges Clement to supply a more qualified alternative, continuing the comparative language of κρείττων."},{"source_quote":"ἡ κρείττων ἀπαρχή","chosen":"the superior firstfruit","rationale":"Retains κρείττων as a comparative description rather than converting it into an English superlative; ‘more excellent firstfruit’ is a possible alternative."},{"source_quote":"ὥσπερ πλέουσιν καὶ κινδυνεύουσιν","chosen":"as people sailing and in danger","rationale":"Retains both the maritime action and the accompanying danger."},{"source_quote":"τὸ κοινῇ πᾶσι συμφέρον","chosen":"what benefits everyone in common","rationale":"Preserves the contrast between Clement’s private interest and the community’s shared good."},{"source_quote":"συνευδοκήσεις","chosen":"you agree with me","rationale":"The compound describes Clement joining Peter in approving and accepting the proposed course."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ὁ δ᾽. ἀπεκρίνατο","issue":"The supplied print places a full stop immediately after the elided δ᾽, syntactically separating ὁ δ᾽ from ἀπεκρίνατο. The translation provisionally reads the words continuously as ‘But he answered.’ This appears to be an editorial punctuation blemish, not evidence of missing text.","proposed_reading":"ὁ δ᾽ ἀπεκρίνατο","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"σὺ γὰρ δι᾽ ἐμοῦ τῶν σωζομένων ἐθνῶν ἡ κρείττων ἀπαρχή","issue":"The attachment of δι᾽ ἐμοῦ is interpretively uncertain. The translation connects it with σωζομένων, yielding ‘the nations being saved through me.’ It can instead modify the main assertion: ‘through me you are the superior firstfruit of the nations being saved.’ The supplied wording requires no textual correction.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"4","text":"“I myself also know, Clement, that I am bestowing on you griefs, discouragements, dangers, and reproaches from uneducated crowds. You will be able to bear these bravely by keeping in view the great reward from God that will be repaid to you for your endurance. But also, as is right, consider together with me: when does the Messiah need your alliance—now, when the evil one has taken up war against his bride, or in the coming time, when, having conquered, he reigns and no longer needs any help? Is it not clear even to someone with little understanding that it is now? Therefore, with full resolve, hurry in this present time of need to ally yourself with a good king, whose nature it is to repay great rewards after victory. Gladly, then, exercise oversight—all the more suitably in this respect, since you have learned from me how to govern the church—for the salvation of the brothers who flee to us for refuge.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"σοι δωρούμενος","chosen":"I am bestowing on you","rationale":"Uses a single gift-related verb for Peter’s act and keeps the griefs, dangers, and reproaches as its objects; the verb pointedly presents the imposed burdens as things bestowed."},{"source_quote":"ἐνορῶν τῆς ὑπομονῆς τὸν ἐκ θεοῦ σοι μέγαν ἀποδιδόμενον μισθόν","chosen":"keeping in view the great reward from God that will be repaid to you for your endurance","rationale":"Preserves the visual orientation of ἐνορῶν and the recompense language of μισθός and ἀποδίδωμι."},{"source_quote":"ὁ χριστός","chosen":"the Messiah","rationale":"Χριστός functions independently as the title of the king whose cause Clement is urged to support."},{"source_quote":"κατὰ τῆς αὐτοῦ νύμφης πόλεμον ἤρατο","chosen":"has taken up war against his bride","rationale":"Keeps both the military action and the bride image without identifying the bride more explicitly than the source does."},{"source_quote":"πάσῃ οὖν προαιρέσει","chosen":"Therefore, with full resolve","rationale":"Προαίρεσις denotes deliberate purpose or resolve, while πάσῃ supplies the comprehensive force represented by ‘full.’"},{"source_quote":"ξυμμαχῆσαι βασιλεῖ ἀγαθῷ","chosen":"to ally yourself with a good king","rationale":"Preserves the political and military alliance imagery rather than generalizing it as mere assistance."},{"source_quote":"ἀποδιδόναι πεφυκότι","chosen":"whose nature it is to repay","rationale":"Conveys πεφυκότι as an established disposition or characteristic of the good king."},{"source_quote":"χαίρων οὖν ἐπισκόπησον","chosen":"Gladly, then, exercise oversight","rationale":"The verb calls Clement to perform episcopal oversight and retains its word-family connection with ἐπίσκοπος without forcing an English denominational formulation."},{"source_quote":"τῶν ἡμῖν προσφευγόντων ἀδελφῶν","chosen":"the brothers who flee to us for refuge","rationale":"Retains the directional movement and protective force of προσφεύγω."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"μισθοὺς μεγάλους· μετὰ νίκην ἀποδιδόναι πεφυκότι","issue":"The printed high point places a strong editorial pause between the object μισθοὺς μεγάλους and the infinitive ἀποδιδόναι on which it depends. The syntax remains recoverable, and the translation provisionally reads the phrase continuously. The proposed reading is conjectural repunctuation only.","proposed_reading":"μισθοὺς μεγάλους μετὰ νίκην ἀποδιδόναι πεφυκότι","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"5","text":"“Nevertheless, before everyone and for everyone’s sake, I also wish to remind you briefly about the matters of governance. You must live blamelessly and, with the greatest diligence, shake off all the occupations of life, becoming neither a guarantor nor an advocate and becoming entangled in no other worldly affair. For the Messiah does not want you appointed as a judge and adjudicator over money or business among the present affairs of worldly life and thereby, absorbed in people’s present concerns, left without leisure to separate, by the word of truth, the better people from the worse. Rather, let those who are learning provide these things for one another, and let them not distract you from the words capable of saving. For just as it is impious for you to undertake worldly concerns while neglecting to do what you were commanded, so it is a sin for each layperson if they do not stand by one another also in worldly needs. Moreover, if all of them do not understand about which matters they ought to keep you free from concern, let them learn from the deacons, so that you may care only for the church, both governing it well and providing the words of truth.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ πάντων διὰ πάντας","chosen":"before everyone and for everyone’s sake","rationale":"Takes ἐπὶ πάντων as indicating the public setting and διὰ πάντας as expressing the concern for everyone that motivates the instruction."},{"source_quote":"πάσας τὰς τοῦ βίου ἀσχολίας ἀποσείεσθαι","chosen":"shake off all the occupations of life","rationale":"Retains the physical force of ἀποσείω and the comprehensive scope of πάσας."},{"source_quote":"μήτε ἐγγυητὴν γινόμενον μήτε συνήγορον","chosen":"becoming neither a guarantor nor an advocate","rationale":"Preserves the distinct financial and legal roles prohibited to the bishop."},{"source_quote":"κριτὴν καὶ δικαστὴν χρημάτων ἢ ἀσχολημάτων","chosen":"a judge and adjudicator over money or business","rationale":"Distinguishes the two judicial terms while treating χρημάτων and ἀσχολημάτων as the financial and business matters over which judgment would be exercised."},{"source_quote":"χωρίζειν λόγῳ ἀληθείας ἀνθρώπων τοὺς κρείττονας ἀπὸ τῶν χειρόνων","chosen":"to separate, by the word of truth, the better people from the worse","rationale":"Retains the source’s language of separation and its comparison between better and worse persons."},{"source_quote":"οἱ μανθάνοντες","chosen":"those who are learning","rationale":"Keeps the expression broader than a fixed institutional label such as ‘catechumens.’"},{"source_quote":"ἑκάστῳ λαϊκῷ","chosen":"for each layperson","rationale":"Λαϊκός distinguishes an ordinary member from the bishop and deacons in the surrounding instructions."},{"source_quote":"περὶ ὧν χρὴ ἀμέριμνον εἶναι οἱ πάντες ποιεῖν","chosen":"about which matters they ought to keep you free from concern","rationale":"Keeps the freedom specifically as freedom from concern about the matters, not freedom from the matters themselves. The placement of χρὴ also permits taking the necessity as applying directly to Clement’s being free from concern."},{"source_quote":"μόνης τῆς ἐκκλησίας τὴν φροντίδα ἔχῃς","chosen":"you may care only for the church","rationale":"Preserves the exclusive force of μόνης and the church as the bishop’s assigned sphere of concern."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"οὐ γὰρ κριτὴν καὶ δικαστὴν χρημάτων ἢ ἀσχολημάτων καθεστάναι σε θέλει τῶν νῦν βιωτικῶν πραγμάτων ὁ χριστός, ἵνα συνεχόμενος εἰς τὰς νῦν τῶν ἀνθρώπων φροντίδας μὴ εὐσχολῇς χωρίζειν λόγῳ ἀληθείας ἀνθρώπων τοὺς κρείττονας ἀπὸ τῶν χειρόνων","issue":"The scope of the unusual οὐ ... θέλει ... ἵνα ... μὴ construction is interpretively difficult. The translation takes the ἵνα clause as the unwanted outcome included within the Messiah’s negated desire: appointment to worldly adjudication would absorb Clement and leave him without leisure for his teaching task. A more formally sequential rendering with ‘so that’ could obscure this scope or suggest that the lack of leisure is the purpose of refusing the appointment. No textual correction is proposed.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"καὶ σὲ δὲ περὶ ὧν χρὴ ἀμέριμνον εἶναι οἱ πάντες ποιεῖν ἐὰν μὴ νοῶσιν, παρὰ τῶν διακόνων μανθανέτωσαν","issue":"The marked word order leaves the relationship of χρὴ to ἀμέριμνον εἶναι and ποιεῖν interpretively uncertain. The translation provisionally understands the necessity as governing the community’s keeping Clement free from concern about certain matters. Alternatively, the phrase may mean that Clement himself ought to be free from concern about those matters and that, if all do not know how to make him so, they should learn from the deacons. This is a syntactic ambiguity in the supplied wording, not evidence of missing or corrupt text.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
